name: Ragi Idli with Coconut-Mint Chutney
desc: Steamed finger millet idlis — calcium and iron-rich, low glycaemic. Served with a no-salt-added coconut chutney blended with mint and green chilli.
steps: Soak urad dal for 4 hours and idli rice for 2 hours. Grind separately to smooth batter. Add ragi flour and mix well. Ferment overnight (8–10 hours) at room temperature.
Add minimal salt (or potassium salt substitute). Pour into greased idli moulds.
Steam for 12 minutes on medium heat. Remove when a skewer comes out clean.
For chutney: blend coconut, mint, green chilli, ginger, and lemon juice to smooth paste with 2 tbsp water. No salt added.
Heat 1 tsp oil in small pan. Splutter mustard seeds, curry leaves and asafoetida. Pour over chutney.
Serve 3 idlis per person with chutney. Add unsalted buttermilk if desired.
dash_notes: Ragi provides 3× more calcium than white rice. Fermentation increases bioavailability of B-vitamins. Coconut chutney without added salt is a key DASH adaptation. Lemon juice enhances iron absorption from ragi.

name: Egg White Oats Pesarattu
desc: Crispy green moong dal crepes fortified with egg whites, served with ginger-tomato chutney. High protein, low saturated fat, DASH-perfect.
steps: Soak moong dal for 3–4 hours. Drain and grind with ginger, green chilli, and cumin to coarse batter. Fold in egg whites.
Heat non-stick tawa on medium-high. Brush with 1 tsp oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread in circular motion. Cook until crisp on edges (2–3 min).
Flip and cook for 1 minute more. Fold and serve.
Chutney: dry-roast garlic and red chilli. Blend with tomato, small amount of tamarind for sourness. No added salt.
dash_notes: Egg whites provide high-quality complete protein without cholesterol of yolks. Moong dal is rich in potassium and magnesium. Garlic in chutney provides allicin — demonstrated vasodilatory effect in RCTs.

name: Kollu (Horsegram) Rasam with Brown Rice & Drumstick Sambar
desc: Traditional horsegram rasam (a BP-lowering staple) with high-fibre brown rice and drumstick moringa sambar — a potassium-magnesium powerhouse.
steps: Cook brown rice (1:2.5 ratio, 35–40 min). Keep warm.
Pressure cook horsegram (6–7 whistles). Save the cooking water for rasam base.
For sambar: pressure cook toor dal and drumstick together. Mash dal. Add tamarind extract, tomato, turmeric, and cook. Season with mustard, curry leaves, dried chilli in minimal oil.
For rasam: use horsegram water, add cumin, black pepper, garlic, tomato, tamarind. Boil for 8 min. Temper with mustard, curry leaves.
Garnish rasam with coriander. Serve 1 cup rice + 1 cup sambar + rasam.
dash_notes: Horsegram is clinically studied for antihypertensive effects (in vitro ACE-inhibitory activity). Drumstick leaves contain isothiocyanates with vasodilatory properties. Brown rice provides 3× more Mg than white rice.

name: Steamed Karimeen (Pearl Spot Fish) with Banana Leaf & Millet Rice
desc: Karimeen steamed in banana leaf with minimal spices — Kerala style. Served with barnyard millet rice and tender coconut water.
steps: Wash fish, make 2–3 diagonal slits on each side. Mix turmeric, pepper, ginger, garlic, lemon juice into a paste. Marinate fish for 20 minutes.
Place fish on cleaned banana leaf. Add green chilli and curry leaves. Fold banana leaf and secure with toothpick.
Steam in idli/dhokla steamer for 15–18 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Cook barnyard millet (1:2 ratio, 20 min) in rice cooker or pot.
Serve banana-leaf steamed fish with millet rice and 200ml fresh tender coconut water.
dash_notes: Karimeen is rich in omega-3 fatty acids — EPA/DHA reduce platelet aggregation and lower BP. Steaming preserves omega-3s and avoids oxidised cooking oils. Coconut water provides 600mg potassium per serving.

name: Roasted Groundnut-Flaxseed Chikki (No Sugar)
desc: DASH-adapted savoury trail mix of roasted groundnuts, flaxseeds, pumpkin seeds, dried curry leaves — bound with minimal jaggery.
steps: Lightly roast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop (2 min). Remove.
Combine all ingredients. Lightly heat jaggery with 1 tsp water to soft-ball stage.
Quickly mix all seeds and nuts into jaggery syrup.
Press onto greased plate and cut into 3 pieces before it hardens.
Alternatively, serve as loose trail mix without jaggery binding.
dash_notes: Flaxseeds provide ALA (plant omega-3) and lignans. Groundnuts contain resveratrol and arginine for NO production. Pumpkin seeds are highest dietary source of magnesium. Only 5mg sodium — virtually zero.

name: Masala Boiled Egg with Cucumber & Amla Juice
desc: Protein-rich boiled egg with BP-lowering amla (Indian gooseberry) juice and cool cucumber slices. A perfect anti-hypertensive mini-meal.
steps: Boil egg for 10 minutes. Peel and slice.
Season with turmeric, black pepper, and lemon juice. No added salt.
Slice cucumber thin.
Dilute amla juice with water. Serve chilled.
Arrange egg slices and cucumber on plate. Serve with amla drink.
dash_notes: Amla is one of highest Vit-C sources (600mg/100g) — antioxidant protection for vascular endothelium. Black pepper + turmeric combination has anti-inflammatory synergy.

name: Ragi Mudde with Mixed Greens Saaru & Low-Fat Curd
desc: Traditional Karnataka staple — ragi balls with light amaranth/methi saaru (soupy gravy). High iron, calcium, and potassium. Classic BP management dinner.
steps: Boil water in heavy-bottomed pan. When boiling, reduce flame and add ragi flour gradually while stirring continuously with wooden spatula.
Cook stirring for 8–10 minutes until mixture forms a solid ball and pulls away from sides. Shape into 2 round balls (mudde).
Pressure cook toor dal. Sauté onion, garlic, tomato in 1 tsp oil with cumin and turmeric.
Add cooked dal, washed greens, and water to make a soupy saaru. Simmer 10 min.
Serve 2 ragi mudde with saaru and 100g low-fat curd. No added salt in curd.
dash_notes: Ragi mudde is the quintessential Karnataka anti-hypertensive meal. Ragi has highest Ca among cereals (344mg/100g). Amaranth leaves have among highest K content of leafy vegetables.

name: Grilled Skinless Chicken Chettinad-Style with Kodo Millet Pulao
desc: Lean skinless chicken marinated in Chettinad spices (no frying) and grilled. Paired with aromatic kodo millet pulao with vegetables.
steps: Mix yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, Chettinad spice blend, lemon juice. Marinate chicken breast for at least 1 hour (refrigerate).
Preheat oven to 200°C or use grill pan. Cook chicken 18–20 min (internal temp 74°C). Rest 5 min before slicing.
For millet pulao: heat oil, add bay leaf, sauté onion until translucent. Add carrot and peas.
Add kodo millet (washed), 1:2 water ratio. Cook covered 20 min on low flame.
Serve sliced grilled chicken over millet pulao. Squeeze fresh lemon.
dash_notes: Skinless chicken breast has 2g saturated fat per 100g — well within DASH limits. Kodo millet has low GI (54) and high magnesium. Homemade Chettinad spice blend avoids commercial mixes with high sodium.

name: Jowar Uttapam with Tomato-Onion Topping
desc: Thick sorghum pancake topped with fresh tomato, onion, and coriander. Naturally gluten-free, high in B-vitamins and potassium.
steps: Mix jowar flour with ground urad dal batter. Add water to achieve thick pourable consistency. Let rest 20 min.
Finely chop tomato, onion, coriander. Mix with green chilli and cumin.
Heat non-stick tawa, pour thick batter, spread to 1.5cm thickness.
Before flipping, scatter tomato-onion mix on top, press lightly.
Cook both sides (3–4 min each) until golden. Drizzle lemon juice before serving.
dash_notes: Jowar (sorghum) is a DASH-ideal grain: high potassium, magnesium, zinc. Tomato provides lycopene — shown to reduce systolic BP. The no-salt topping with fresh vegetables maximises potassium:sodium ratio.

name: Sardine Akuri (Spiced Scrambled) on Jowar Toast
desc: Omega-3 rich sardines gently scrambled with eggs, onion, green chilli and minimal spice on toasted jowar bread. Clinical BP management breakfast.
steps: Drain and rinse sardines (reduces sodium by ~40%). Flake with fork.
Sauté onion in oil for 2 min. Add tomato, green chilli, turmeric.
Add sardines and egg whites. Scramble on medium heat, 3–4 min.
Season with black pepper. No added salt.
Toast jowar bread. Top with sardine-egg mixture. Garnish with coriander.
dash_notes: Sardines are one of the highest omega-3 sources affordable in South India. Rinsing canned sardines reduces sodium by up to 40%. Egg whites add protein without cholesterol.

name: Avial with Red Rice & Moong Dal Soup
desc: Kerala-style avial — 7 vegetables in coconut-yoghurt gravy — with high-antioxidant Palakkadan Matta (red) rice and thin moong dal.
steps: Cook red rice (1:3 ratio, 40–45 min). Red rice requires longer cooking.
Cut all vegetables uniformly (3cm pieces). Parboil drumstick and yam first (5 min).
Grind coconut with green chilli and cumin coarsely.
Cook all vegetables in minimal water. When almost done, add coconut mixture.
Remove from heat, fold in yoghurt. Add curry leaves. Finish with 1 tsp coconut oil.
Boil moong dal with turmeric, temper with cumin. Serve all three together.
dash_notes: Avial with 7 vegetables is a DASH gold standard — potassium from drumstick + yam + banana is extraordinary (>700mg/serving). Red rice has 3× the polyphenols of white rice.

name: Prawn Kolambu with Thinai (Foxtail Millet) Rice
desc: Spiced prawn curry with minimum coconut, tomato-tamarind base, served with low-GI foxtail millet rice. High lean protein, omega-3.
steps: Cook thinai millet (1:2.5 ratio, 20 min).
Heat oil, splutter mustard. Add curry leaves, onion. Sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 2 min. Add tomatoes, cook until mushy.
Add all dry spice powders, turmeric. Cook masala for 3 min.
Add tamarind water (soak tamarind, extract liquid). Simmer 5 min.
Add cleaned prawns. Cook 5–7 min until pink and curled. Garnish with coriander.
dash_notes: Prawns are low in saturated fat and high in lean protein. Thinai (foxtail millet) has GI ~50 and is high in silica for vascular health. Tamarind replaces salt as souring agent.

name: Cucumber-Pomegranate Raita with Chia Seeds
desc: Cooling raita with hypertension-fighting pomegranate arils, cucumber, and omega-3 rich chia seeds. A clinical superfood in disguise.
steps: Soak chia seeds in 2 tbsp water for 10 minutes until gel forms.
Whisk curd smooth. Fold in cucumber, pomegranate arils, soaked chia.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black pepper. No salt.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves. Serve chilled.
dash_notes: Pomegranate is among the most clinically studied fruits for BP reduction — punicalagins inhibit ACE enzyme. Chia seeds add omega-3 ALA. Yoghurt provides calcium and GABA with mild hypotensive effect.

name: Chicken Tikka Skewers (No Cream) with Mint Chutney
desc: Lean chicken tikka without cream — marinated in spiced yoghurt, grilled. Protein-dense, virtually zero carbohydrate snack.
steps: Mix yoghurt, ginger, garlic, all spice powders, lemon juice into marinade. No added salt.
Cube chicken, add to marinade. Refrigerate 1–2 hours.
Thread onto skewers. Grill/oven-roast at 220°C for 15 min, turning halfway.
Mint chutney: blend mint, green chilli, garlic, lemon juice — no salt.
Serve 4 tikka skewers with mint chutney.
dash_notes: DASH-adapted version removes cream and added salt from standard tikka. Lemon juice as souring agent replaces sodium. Only 135mg sodium makes this suitable for strict DASH phase.

name: Pesarattu with Allam (Ginger) Chutney & Vegetable Upma
desc: Green moong dal pesarattu with fiery ginger chutney plus a light vegetable upma with cracked wheat. Andhra Pradesh classic, DASH-adapted.
steps: Grind soaked moong dal with minimal water to coarse batter.
Make pesarattu: heat non-stick tawa, pour ladle of batter, spread thin. Cook crisp (3 min), flip (1 min). Make 3 pesarattu.
Ginger chutney: dry roast ginger, red chilli. Grind with tamarind, jaggery to paste. No salt.
Upma: temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves. Add onion, vegetables. Sauté 4 min. Add cracked wheat, 2:1 water. Cover, cook 12 min.
Serve pesarattu with chutney alongside upma.
dash_notes: Pesarattu is native Andhra protein-rich crepe. Moong dal is highest legume source of potassium per calorie. Ginger contains 6-gingerol — shown in clinical trials to reduce SBP by ~6mmHg.

name: Vanjaram (Seer Fish) Varuval with Millet Kitchadi
desc: Tawa-grilled seer fish varuval (spice-rubbed) — light, anti-inflammatory. Served with mixed millet dal kitchadi.
steps: Marinate fish fillet with turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice. Rest 20 min.
Heat 2 tsp oil in flat pan. Grill fish 4–5 min each side until golden crust forms. No deep frying.
Kitchadi: dry roast mixed millets. Pressure cook with moong dal, carrots, peas, cumin (1:3 water ratio, 3–4 whistles).
Temper kitchadi with cumin. Squeeze lemon over fish before serving.
dash_notes: Vanjaram (Spanish mackerel) is one of highest omega-3 fish available in South India. Tawa frying with minimal oil retains omega-3s vs deep frying. Mixed millet kitchadi is an exceptional magnesium source.

name: Rajma Tikki on Ragi Bread with Amla Pickle
desc: Kidney bean patties on ragi bread — plant-based, BP-lowering, potassium-rich. With amla-based low-sodium pickle.
steps: Mash cooked rajma coarsely. Mix in onion, ginger, spice powders, lemon juice, ragi flour.
Shape into 4 flat tikkis. Pan-fry in 1 tsp oil on non-stick pan, 3 min each side until crisp.
Toast ragi bread.
Serve 2 tikkis on ragi toast with amla pickle.
dash_notes: Rajma contains anthocyanins shown to reduce SBP. Kidney beans are highest potassium legume per serving. Amla pickle without salt provides Vit-C and gallic acid — both endothelium-protective.

name: Moringa (Murungai Keerai) Kootu with Sambar & Brown Rice
desc: Moringa leaf stir-fry with lentils (kootu) — one of the most nutrient-dense dishes on the planet. Rich in potassium, calcium, iron and quercetin.
steps: Cook brown rice.
Pressure cook chana dal (2 whistles). Drain, keep aside.
Sauté onion in 1 tsp oil. Add moringa leaves (remove from stem), cook 5 min.
Grind coconut with green chilli and cumin. Add to moringa-dal mixture. Cook 5 min (kootu).
Make sambar: cook toor dal, add tomato, tamarind, temper with mustard-curry leaves.
Serve rice + kootu + sambar.
dash_notes: Moringa has 3× the potassium of bananas and 17× the calcium of milk per gram. Isothiocyanates and quercetin in moringa are potent vasodilators studied in multiple RCTs. Highest DASH score (98) in database.

name: Mutton Paya Soup (Light) with Jowar Bhakri
desc: Bone broth paya (trotter) soup — collagen-rich, mineral-dense. Prepared lean with minimal fat. Served with jowar bhakri (unleavened bread).
steps: Clean trotters thoroughly. Pressure cook with whole spices, ginger, and garlic for 8–10 whistles until very tender.
Remove fat that floats on top (skim carefully). This reduces saturated fat significantly.
Sauté onion in 1 tsp oil. Add coriander powder, cumin. Add to strained broth.
Simmer 15 min. Garnish with coriander.
Jowar bhakri: mix jowar flour with warm water to stiff dough. Roll thick (5mm). Roast on tawa without oil.
dash_notes: Bone broth provides glycine, proline and hydroxyproline — supporting vascular collagen. Fat skimming is essential to reduce saturated fat. Limit to once per week.

name: Banana-Sesame Smoothie with Fenugreek Powder
desc: Potassium-packed banana with calcium-rich sesame seeds and BP-lowering fenugreek powder — blended into a thick smoothie.
steps: Blend banana, milk, ground sesame seeds, fenugreek powder, cardamom.
Add ice and blend again until smooth.
Serve immediately — sesame fat oxidises quickly.
dash_notes: Bananas provide 422mg potassium each. Sesame (til) is highest calcium food in Indian cuisine (975mg/100g). Fenugreek contains diosgenin which reduces aldosterone-mediated sodium retention.

name: Palak (Spinach) Moong Dal Khichdi with Buttermilk
desc: One-pot meal of spinach, yellow moong dal and rice. Complete protein + iron + folate combination. Light, easily digestible DASH dinner.
steps: Wash dal and rice. Pressure cook together (1:3.5 ratio, 3 whistles) until mushy.
Blanch spinach briefly (1 min boiling water), squeeze, chop.
Mix spinach into khichdi, cook 5 min stirring.
Temper with cumin seeds in ghee (1 small tsp).
Season with turmeric, lemon juice. No added salt.
Serve with cold unsalted buttermilk.
dash_notes: Spinach provides folate, iron, nitrates (endogenous NO precursor) and potassium. Inorganic nitrates in leafy greens are established vasodilators — 200g spinach provides ~150mg nitrates, equivalent to ~5mmHg SBP reduction.

name: Meen Molee (Prawn in Coconut Milk) with Brown Rice
desc: Light Kerala meen molee with tiger prawns in thin coconut milk — gentler than dense curries, higher omega-3. DASH-adapted with reduced coconut.

ingredients.name: Light coconut milk (1:1 diluted with water)

steps: Cook brown rice.
Heat oil, sauté onion, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves until soft (5 min).
Add turmeric and tomato. Cook until tomato softens.
Add diluted coconut milk. Simmer on low heat (do not boil).
Add prawns, cook 6–8 min until pink. Finish with lemon juice.
Garnish with coriander. Serve over brown rice.
dash_notes: Diluting coconut milk 1:1 halves saturated fat while maintaining flavour. Tiger prawns are higher in omega-3 than other prawns. Brown rice vs white rice adds 2g more fibre per serving.

name: Oat-Banana Dosa with Guava-Mint Chutney
desc: Instant oat-banana dosa — no fermentation needed. Beta-glucan from oats + potassium from banana + Vit-C from guava chutney.
steps: Blend oats to coarse flour. Mash banana. Mix oat flour, banana, rice flour, curd, ginger, green chilli. Add water for pouring consistency.
Let batter rest 10 minutes.
Pour thin dosa on hot tawa. Cook 2–3 min crisp, flip 1 min.
Chutney: blend guava, mint, lemon juice. No salt added.
Make 4 small dosas. Serve with guava-mint chutney.
dash_notes: Oat beta-glucan reduces LDL cholesterol and has mild BP-lowering effects. Banana provides additional potassium. Guava has among highest Vit-C content of South Indian fruits (228mg/100g).

name: Rajasthani Dal Baati (DASH-Adapted) with Millet Roti
desc: Tri-dal (toor, moong, chana) thick soup with minimal ghee, served with multi-millet roti. High plant protein, fibre, and potassium.
steps: Pressure cook mixed dals (2–3 whistles). Mash partially.
Prepare millet roti: mix millet flour blend with warm water to pliable dough. Roll into thick rotis. Roast on tawa, both sides.
For dal: sauté onion, garlic, ginger in 1 tsp oil. Add tomato, spices. Add cooked dal, thin with water. Simmer 10 min.
Add 1 tsp ghee for finish.
Serve with lemon juice squeezed over dal.
dash_notes: Combining three lentils (toor+moong+chana) provides complementary amino acid profiles. Millet blend roti provides Mg from bajra (150mg/100g), Ca from ragi. Highest fiber meal at 11.2g per serving.

name: Jamun (Java Plum) & Groundnut Salad
desc: Seasonal jamun with roasted groundnuts and lemon dressing — anthocyanin-rich, BP-lowering afternoon snack.
steps: Wash jamun, remove seeds, halve.
Combine jamun, cucumber, groundnuts.
Dress with lemon juice, black pepper, minimal chaat masala.
Serve immediately (jamun oxidises).
dash_notes: Jamun (Syzygium cumini) has the highest anthocyanin content of South Indian fruits. Anthocyanins reduce ACE activity and improve endothelial function. Only 8mg sodium — lowest in the database.

name: Kerala Green Coconut Curry with Ash Gourd & Barley
desc: Ishtew-inspired light coconut curry with ash gourd (winter melon) — cooling, diuretic, BP-friendly. With pearled barley (high beta-glucan).
steps: Cook pearled barley (1:3 ratio, 30–35 min) until tender.
Cube ash gourd and potato. Cook in water until half-done (8 min).
Add sliced shallots, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves. Continue cooking.
Add diluted coconut milk, coriander. Simmer gently 5 min (do not boil hard).
Finish with coconut oil (1 tsp for authentic flavour).
Serve over barley.
dash_notes: Ash gourd (white pumpkin) has mild diuretic properties. Barley has strongest evidence for BP reduction among grains — beta-glucan content (3g/serving) is a recognised functional component.

name: Thinai (Foxtail Millet) Pongal with Pepper Ghee
desc: South Indian creamy pongal using foxtail millet instead of rice. Comfort food with BP-lowering black pepper, low sodium.
steps: Dry roast foxtail millet and moong dal together for 3 min until fragrant.
Pressure cook together (1:3.5 ratio, 3 whistles) until creamy.
Heat ghee in small pan. Add cumin, black pepper, curry leaves, ginger, asafoetida. Splutter 1 min.
Pour tempering over pongal. Mix well. Adjust consistency with hot water.
Garnish with lightly roasted cashews. Serve hot.
dash_notes: Black pepper — piperine — inhibits voltage-gated calcium channels (similar mechanism to calcium channel blocker antihypertensives). Foxtail millet has lower GI than rice pongal and provides more magnesium.

name: Fish Cutlets (Baked) with Tomato Chutney
desc: Kerala-style fish cutlets baked (not fried) with minimal potato, served with fresh tomato-garlic chutney on jowar toast.
steps: Mix flaked fish, mashed potato, onion, ginger-garlic, green chilli, coriander, spices.
Shape into 4 flat cutlets. Dip in egg white, coat with whole wheat breadcrumbs.
Place on greased baking tray. Bake 200°C for 18–20 min, flip halfway.
Tomato chutney: roast garlic, blend with tomato, black pepper, lemon. No salt.
Serve 2 cutlets on jowar toast with chutney.
dash_notes: Baking cutlets vs deep-frying reduces fat by ~70%. Tomato chutney provides lycopene — heat-activated antioxidant with BP-lowering properties. Whole-wheat breadcrumbs add fibre.

name: Broccoli-Carrot Upkari with Rice & Coconut Kadhi
desc: Mangalorean udupi-style stir-fry (upkari) of broccoli and carrot in mustard-coconut tempering with cooling coconut kadhi.
steps: Cook brown rice.
Upkari: heat oil, splutter mustard, urad dal, curry leaves, dried red chilli. Add blanched broccoli and sliced carrot. Stir-fry 5–6 min. Add coconut, lemon, toss.
Kadhi: blend curd with grated coconut, ginger, green chilli, cumin. Thin with water. Heat gently without boiling. No salt.
Serve rice, upkari, and kadhi together.
dash_notes: Broccoli provides sulforaphane — activates Nrf2 pathway, reducing vascular oxidative stress. Carrot provides beta-carotene and potassium. Udupi cuisine is naturally DASH-compatible.

name: Chettinad Chicken Kulambu with Samba Heritage Rice
desc: Authentic Chettinad chicken curry — rich in kalpasi (stone flower), marathi mokku, kapok buds — complex aromatic spices. With samba heritage rice.
steps: Dry roast Chettinad spices (kalpasi, marathi mokku, star anise, fennel, coriander, red chilli) and grind to powder.
Cook samba rice.
Sauté shallots in oil until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato, cook until oil separates. Add ground Chettinad masala.
Add chicken pieces, coat well. Add water, cook covered 25 min until tender.
Add curry leaves, simmer 5 min. Serve with samba rice.
dash_notes: Chettinad spice palette includes kalpasi (anti-inflammatory properties). Fennel contains anethole with smooth-muscle relaxation properties. Shallots are richer in quercetin than regular onions.

name: Orange-Flaxseed Lassi (No Sugar)
desc: Refreshing blend of low-fat curd, fresh orange juice, and ground flaxseeds. Probiotic + omega-3 + Vit-C anti-hypertensive snack.
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth and frothy.
Serve immediately (flaxseed oxidises if left standing).
dash_notes: Orange provides hesperidin — a flavonoid with proven SBP-lowering effect (12-week RCT). Curd provides calcium and GABA. Flaxseed powder provides ALA omega-3 and SDG lignans (both with BP-lowering evidence).

name: Mangalorean Crab Ghee Roast (DASH-Adapted) with Dosa
desc: Iconic Mangalore crab roast — DASH-adapted with reduced butter, extra tomato-tamarind base. Served with thin rice-lentil dosa.
steps: Dry roast Kashmiri chilli, coriander, cumin, pepper. Grind with garlic and tamarind to paste.
Heat ghee+oil mixture. Sauté the masala paste until fragrant and oil separates (5–6 min).
Add crab, coat with masala. Add jaggery, curry leaves. Roast on medium-high heat 10–12 min, tossing frequently.
Make thin dosa from prepared batter in non-stick pan.
dash_notes: Crab is lean seafood with high zinc, selenium, and B12. This DASH-adapted version halves the ghee vs traditional recipe. Kashmiri chilli gives colour without excessive heat. Consumed once weekly maximum.

name: Bajra Khichdi with Lauki (Bottle Gourd) & Coriander Chutney
desc: Pearl millet-dal khichdi with bottle gourd — one of the most BP-lowering combinations. Lauki is a proven Ayurvedic antihypertensive vegetable.
steps: Wash bajra and dal. Soak bajra 30 min for faster cooking.
Pressure cook bajra, dal, diced lauki, ginger together (4–5 whistles).
Heat ghee, splutter cumin. Add turmeric. Pour over khichdi.
Coriander chutney: blend fresh coriander, green chilli, lemon juice, ginger. No salt.
Serve khichdi with chutney.
dash_notes: Bottle gourd (lauki) juice is a validated Ayurvedic antihypertensive studied in clinical trials. Its high water content and choline reduce BP via diuretic effect. Bajra has highest potassium among millets (307mg/100g).

name: Bisibele Bath (DASH-Adapted) with Raita
desc: Karnataka iconic one-pot rice-lentil-vegetable dish, DASH-adapted with millet substitution, reduced ghee, and no pickle.

ingredients.name: Bisibele bath spice powder (homemade, no salt)

steps: Pressure cook dal and rice-millet blend separately. Mix together.
Cook vegetables in water until just tender. Add to rice-dal.
Homemade BBB powder: roast and grind coriander, cumin, dried red chilli, cloves, cinnamon, kalpasi (no salt in powder).
Add tamarind, jaggery, tomato, BBB powder to rice-dal-veg mixture. Simmer 15 min, stirring.
Temper with ghee, mustard, curry leaves, cashews. Pour over and mix.
Serve with raita.
dash_notes: Bisibele bath is a DASH near-perfect meal when homemade. Store-bought mixes are high in sodium — homemade powder avoids this. Millet substitution adds Mg and fibre. Combination of toor dal + brown rice + millets provides complete protein.

name: Hibiscus-Ginger Iced Tea with Sesame Ladoo
desc: Hibiscus tea (proven ACE inhibitor effect) with mini jaggery-sesame ladoo. Evidence-based snack for BP management.
steps: Steep hibiscus flowers and ginger in hot water 8–10 min. Strain.
Add lemon juice. Cool, then refrigerate or serve over ice.
Sesame ladoo: dry roast sesame until golden. Melt jaggery with 1 tsp water to soft-ball stage. Mix sesame and cardamom into jaggery. Shape into 2 small balls quickly. Cool.
Serve tea with 2 sesame ladoos.
dash_notes: Hibiscus sabdariffa tea has strong clinical evidence for BP reduction (>10 RCTs). The anthocyanins inhibit ACE enzyme activity and reduce angiotensin II. Studies show 65mg/day can reduce SBP by 7.2mmHg. Only 10mg sodium.

name: Pepper Duck Varuval (Lean) with Rice Congee
desc: Kerala-style duck varuval with lean breast meat only, heavy on pepper and ginger, light on oil. With light rice congee for easy digestion.
steps: Score duck breast. Marinate with crushed black pepper, half the ginger, lemon juice, turmeric for 30 min.
Cook rice congee: boil rice in 5× water ratio until porridge consistency. Season with minimal ginger.
Heat coconut oil, sauté shallots, fennel, remaining ginger until golden.
Add duck, sear on high heat 3–4 min each side. Reduce heat, cook 12–15 min (internal 74°C).
Slice duck, top with fried curry leaves. Serve with congee.
dash_notes: Duck breast without skin is comparable to chicken in saturated fat. Black pepper in large amounts (6g) is therapeutic — piperine inhibits ACE. Congee (rice gruel) is easy to digest and soothing.

name: Lemon-Turmeric Sevai (Rice Noodles) with Groundnut Chutney
desc: Light steamed rice noodles tossed in lemon and turmeric with curry leaf tempering. Anti-inflammatory, easy to digest, potassium-rich.
steps: Steam rice sevai as per package. Fluff gently.
Heat oil, splutter mustard. Add curry leaves, green chilli, turmeric.
Add turmeric first to oil, then add cooked sevai, lemon juice. Toss gently.
Groundnut chutney: blend roasted groundnuts with green chilli, ginger, lemon. No salt.
Garnish with coconut and coriander. Serve with chutney.
dash_notes: Curcumin in turmeric has vasodilatory effects via NO pathway. Lemon juice adds Vit-C with zero sodium. Lowest-calorie breakfast in the plan (215kcal) — suitable for elderly individuals.

name: Egg Kothu Parota (Millet, DASH Version) with Onion Sambar
desc: Street-food favourite kothu parota reinvented with millet parotas, limited egg, and minimal oil. Served with thin onion sambar.
steps: Prepare millet parotas: mix millet-wheat blend flour (60:40), make soft dough, roll, fold into layers, cook in 1 tsp oil on tawa. Cool.
Heat oil in flat iron griddle or wok. Sauté onion, capsicum, curry leaves.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato. Cook 3 min. Push to side.
Beat eggs, scramble in centre. Mix all together.
Add torn millet parota pieces. Toss with spoons/spatulas on high heat 3–4 min.
Serve with thin onion sambar.
dash_notes: Millet parota replaces refined maida — reduces GI significantly. No added salt, relies on garam masala (aromatic) and lemon for flavour. Once-weekly, this meets DASH standards. Excellent protein from 2 eggs.

name: Pongal Sundal Festival Thali — 7 Dal/Legume Sundal
desc: Celebratory South Indian festival thali — 7 different sundals (legume stir-fries). Rich in potassium, protein, fibre. Perfect Sunday meal.

ingredients.name: Mustard, curry leaves, red chilli (per sundal)

steps: Pre-soak and pressure cook all legumes separately (or use canned, rinsed well).
For each sundal: heat 1/4 tsp oil, splutter mustard, curry leaves, dried red chilli. Add cooked legume, 1 tsp grated coconut, lemon squeeze. Toss and serve.
Cook brown rice separately.
Arrange 7 small sundals in individual katoris around rice in a thali.
dash_notes: 7 different legumes provides full spectrum of amino acids, flavonoids, and minerals. Total potassium of 780mg in this meal alone — highest in database. Each legume has different anthocyanin/polyphenol profile.

name: Nethili (Anchovies) Fry with Tamarind Rice & Kootu
desc: Crispy nethili (anchovies) — calcium powerhouse, whole fish eaten including bones. With tamarind rice and vegetable kootu.
steps: Clean nethili, marinate with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder (no salt). Shallow fry in sesame oil 4–5 min until crispy.
Cook rice. Prepare tamarind rice: heat sesame oil, splutter mustard, curry leaves, groundnuts. Add tamarind extract. Toss rice.
Drumstick kootu: cook drumstick with toor dal, coconut, cumin tempered.
Serve together as traditional Tamil Nadu thali.
dash_notes: Nethili/anchovies eaten whole: calcium content is exceptional (438mg/100g — higher than milk). Omega-3 (EPA+DHA) at 900mg/100g. Sesame oil contains sesamin with antihypertensive properties.

name: Tender Coconut with Sprouts Chaat
desc: Tender coconut water (highest natural K source) with iron-rich mixed sprouts chaat dressed with lemon and chaat masala.
steps: Lightly steam sprouts (2 min) to reduce antinutrients. Cool.
Mix sprouts with onion, tomato, coriander.
Dress with lemon juice, homemade chaat masala. No added salt.
Serve alongside tender coconut water.
dash_notes: Tender coconut water contains 600mg potassium per serving — highest natural potassium beverage. Sprouting increases potassium, Vit-C. Methi sprouts contain diosgenin with aldosterone-blocking properties. Total potassium: 680mg.

name: Tiger Prawn Masala with Ragi Dosa (Sunday Special)
desc: Weekend special — tiger prawn masala in minimal coconut, generous spices. With crispy ragi dosa. A DASH-compliant celebration meal.
steps: Ragi dosa batter: mix ragi flour and urad dal batter with water to thin consistency. Rest 20 min.
Masala: sauté shallots in oil until deep golden. Add ginger-garlic.
Grind kalpasi, marathi mokku, fennel coarsely. Add to pan with coriander powder, red chilli.
Add tomato, cook until oil separates. Add prawns, coat well.
Add light coconut milk, cook 8–10 min until prawns cooked and gravy thickened.
Make thin ragi dosas on hot tawa. Serve with prawn masala.
dash_notes: Ragi dosa is high Ca and Fe. Shallots have higher quercetin than onions — important flavonoid for cardiovascular protection. Light coconut milk (diluted) keeps saturated fat within weekly limits. Sunday special to maintain dietary adherence.
